newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: IGNALINA BORROWS FROM BANK OF NEW YORK.
newsitem.headline: IGNALINA BORROWS FROM BANK OF NEW YORK.

text.p: The Bank of New York signed on Thursday a $9.9 million soft loan agreement in Vilnius with Ignalina nuclear power plant to upgrade its computer system.
The U.S. EXIM bank will act as credit guarantor and the government also guaranteed the credit, the director of Ignalina Viktor Shevaldin said during the signing ceremony.
"The whole project needs $11.5 million and a part of it, 15 percent, was made by Ignalina," Shevaldin said.
Shevaldin also said the computer upgrading works should be finished by the end of 1998 and then the repayments for the credit will start.
"We will start the repayments in 2000 and will pay for five years," Shevaldin said.
"The terms of the contract are very favourable for us and the interest rate for the credit is a little bit over five percent, only a grant could be cheaper," Shevaldin added.
"The repayment for the credit starts as soon as the last shipment of equipment is done and everything is installed," said assistant to the vice president of the Bank of New York, Georg Knoth.
"Then the loan is consolidated and then we'll have five years repayment period with ten semi annual payments," Knoth told Reuters.
Ignalina has so far received around 10 million marks in credit from German Kredit fur Wiederaufbau to acquire waste fuel containers, Shevaldin said.
The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) granted 35 million ECU, of which 70 percent has been used.
The Swedish government's help to Ignalina is estimated at around $25 million, Shevaldin said.
